notes: This paper studies Kelpak SL seaweed extract on a grass mixture (Dactylis glomerata and Festulolium braunii cultivars) in a 3-year experiment (2010-2012) with 3 cuts per year. The GT has only 3 rows corresponding to cuts 1, 2, and 3 with small absolute values (ctrl: 1.33, 1.06, 0.83 t ha-1) that do not match any single JSON obs directly — all JSON per-cut yields are 1.9-5.3 t ha-1. This ~3-4x discrepancy in absolute means suggests Li 2022 either (a) averaged across all 4 cultivars and divided by number of years yielding a different aggregation, or (b) extracted from a different summary table not captured in our JSON obs. Effect sizes are partially consistent: cut 3 effect matches well (GT +7.23% vs JSON Amila cut 3 +7.14%), cuts 1-2 are less well matched. Matches are assigned by cut number ordering (GT pairs 514/515/516 = cuts 1/2/3) with low-to-medium confidence due to the absolute mean discrepancy. The JSON contains many non-yield forage quality observations (N, NDF, ADF content) that are correctly excluded from matching.
